- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid excessive overshoot.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above or below 30-day moving average, adjust toward it by 1–3% in next period.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; dampen initial forecast by 1–2%.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-window, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or add a 1–2% downward bias after sentiment drop.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model often overestimates; apply 0.5–1.5% downward correction to avoid false momentum.
